lessons.title: Confidence-Interval Logic and Interpretation
lessons.focus: distinguishing the long-run success rate of a method from probability statements about a fixed parameter
lessons.essential: How do confidence intervals combine an estimate, standard error, confidence level, and design assumptions?
lessons.application: polling, manufacturing, medicine, environmental monitoring, education, and business analytics
lessons.p1: Give one defensible analysis step for Confidence-Interval Logic and Interpretation.
lessons.s1: State the question and data structure, apply distinguishing the long-run success rate of a method from probability statements about a fixed parameter, check assumptions or design conditions, quantify uncertainty, and interpret the result in context.
lessons.p2: Identify a common error in Confidence-Interval Logic and Interpretation.
lessons.s2: A common error is to report a calculation without identifying the population, design, assumptions, uncertainty, context, or limits on causal and generalizing claims.
